newsitem.title: USA: Clinton casts ballot, awaits election returns.
newsitem.headline: Clinton casts ballot, awaits election returns.

text.p: President Bill Clinton voted at a polling place in his hometown's renovated train station on Tuesday, then joined family and friends to await his expected triumph over Republican Bob Dole.

Accompanied by his wife, Hillary, and their 16-year-old daughter, Chelsea, Clinton cast his paper ballot at just after midday. He smiled broadly and waved to onlookers as he entered the station on the edge of downtown Little Rock, two blocks from the state capitol building.

As he emerged back into the bright sunlight after voting, Clinton hugged and kissed Chelsea and exchanged an exuberant high-five handslap with his daughter before entering his limousine and driving away.

The Clintons flew to Little Rock aboard Air Force One at 3:33 a.m. EST, closing out a grueling campaign season that unofficially began more than a year ago. Their emotional return to a state Clinton led as governor for 12 years followed a raucous late-night rally in Sioux City, South Dakota, the last stop on a 20-hour, six-state election-eve barnstorming tour.
"This is the greatest country in human history because we have created a system in which you are the boss," Clinton said in asking voters to renew his contract for four more years.

Unlike the sense of grim determination that characterised the presidential party that accompanied then-incumbent George Bush to Houston four years ago to await the election results, Clinton and his clan reflected joyful anticipation.
Enroute to Little Rock from South Dakota, the president and first lady toasted their staff and Secret Service agents who have been away from home so often because of the campaign.

Clinton and his aides also danced the macarena, a loose-limbed Latin line dance that Democrats have adopted as their celebratory war dance. Asked to evaluate the commander-in-chief's performance, White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Clinton had done the macarena "in a presidential manner."

Clinton led Dole by 11 percentage points in a final CNN/USA TODAY/Gallup Poll released on Tuesday. The poll of 1,488 likely voters, with a margin of error of plus or minus three points, gave Clinton a lead of 52 to 41 percent over Dole. Reform Party candidate Ross Perot received 7 percent.
Asked whom they would vote for in congressional races, 49.5 percent favoured Democratic candidates in their districts while 50.5 favoured Republicans.

A top Clinton campaign aide was doubtful he would achieve his goal of becoming a majority president by getting 50 percent of the vote. "I think we'll be just under it," the aide told Reuters. Clinton won with 43 percent in 1992.

The fate of the Republican-controlled Congress was far from clear. Although much of Clinton's popularity in the past two years can be traced to his opposition to the Republican agenda, it was unclear whether his coattails would benefit fellow Democrats.
"We have a good shot at winning back the House of Representatives but the Senate is out of reach," the aide said.

Little Rock city officials were busy preparing a huge election-night street party, closing off downtown streets around the Old State House, a large Greek Revival structure where as many as 80,000 people are expected to congregate.

When Clinton was elected president in 1992, it was on the front steps of the historic building, which once served as the state capitol, where he claimed victory before 50,000 people. He planned to do the same again this year.

Vice President Al Gore and his wife Tipper planned to vote in Tennessee and then fly with their children to Little Rock to join the Clintons in awaiting election results. The ticket has a substantial lead in enough states that Clinton and Gore are likely to be projected as winners by early evening.
Virtually all 6,000 hotel rooms in metropolitan Little Rock were taken and utility workers have added electrical circuits and telephone lines to handle the expected surge in demand.

Rock stars Stephen Stills and Nicolette Larson and country singer Kathy Mattea were to play at the Riverfront Ampitheatre and TV images of the events and network election returns will be projected on huge screens throughout the downtown area.
